tools.name: report
tools.description: Report something you did to the people watching this session: progress on a long task (at milestones), an artifact such as a pull request (with its url), a handoff to another crew member (with to), a tool refused or an error. One short line.

op.description: file: what you did to it

to.description: handoff: the member the work goes to

tool.description: tool_use, tool_denied, error, file: the tool involved

tools.name: set_state
tools.description: Tell the people watching that you are working, done, or clear the state; use ask for a question.

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask the people watching for a decision you cannot make yourself; the session shows as needing input until someone answers in the terminal, also once your turn has ended. With choices (at most 6, each at most 40 characters), name them in the terminal too: a click types the choice as a line. If you no longer need the answer, clear the question with set_state clear.

tools.name: form_crew
tools.description: Form a crew around this session when the work splits into parts that can run side by side: you stay as the member named by self (its agentId and prompt may be empty), the others get sessions of their own. At most 2 a session; never for work you can finish alone.

open.description: offer the run in the workbench

tools.name: add_member
tools.description: Add a member to this session's run: {name, agentId, prompt, start}.

tools.name: run_status
tools.description: This session's run and its members, with their states.

tools.name: link
tools.description: A view-only link to this session, for a pull request or a message; a day at most.

tools.name: task_context
tools.description: Your task, when this session is an attempt at a task of a managed run (CONDUCTOR_TASK is set): the goal, the task, where it starts and its inputs, findings to address, how it is checked and how to submit. The same text is .conductor/task.md in your working directory. Long tasks come in pages of 32 KiB: page 1 unless given.

tools.name: task_result
tools.description: Submit your attempt's result, once. A work task: commit your work first (the worktree must be clean apart from .conductor/), then give a summary, the issues you know of, and the commit (HEAD unless given). A review: do not commit; give the verdict, approved or needs_changes, with findings {severity: blocker|major|minor|nit, path, line, message}. Conductor checks the commit and decides the task; a refusal says what to fix before you submit again. The same commit submitted twice is taken once. A done or a handoff does not finish a task; only this does.

commit.description: the result commit, the full id; HEAD when not given

issues.description: what is left or doubtful, one line each

summary.description: what you did, one paragraph, at most 4000 characters

tools.name: message_send
tools.description: In a managed run, send another member a message: kept with the run and typed into that member's session as one line ("Message from <you> (#n): …") once its attempt has its task; a member not started yet gets it then. A member keeps at most 50 messages not acknowledged. Use it for what the next task needs to know beyond your result; a result is still submitted with task_result.

tools.name: inbox_read
tools.description: In a managed run, your messages from the other members, in order: each with its sequence number, who sent it and whether it was typed into your session. Pass after to read past what you have seen.

after.description: the last sequence number read; 0 for all

tools.name: inbox_ack
tools.description: In a managed run, acknowledge your messages up to a sequence number: they count no more against your inbox.

tools.name: task_blocked
tools.description: In a managed run, say what stops your attempt at its task: a missing credential, a decision, something to be done by hand. The people watching see the task as blocked with the reason, and your session asks them the message (else the reason) as your question; reporting working or done, or submitting, clears it.

message.description: what you need from the people watching, at most 4000 characters

reason.description: what blocks you, one line of at most 500 characters

tools.name: task_checkpoint
tools.description: In a managed run, save where your attempt got to, tied to the commit your worktree is at (commit first): what is done, what remains, notes. The next attempt at the task reads it in its task file, and one after an attempt that ends without a result starts at that commit, so the work is not lost.

done.description: what is done, at most 4000 characters

notes.description: anything the next attempt should know

tools.name: ticket_read
tools.description: The Dispatch ticket your run is linked to, when a person linked it to one: its key and title, status, priority, owner, labels, description, acceptance criteria, close policy, links and last comments. Read it for what was asked and how it is accepted. A run belongs to one ticket at most; with none, the tool says so.

tools.name: ticket_comment
tools.description: Comment on the Dispatch ticket your run is linked to, for the people who own it: what you found, what you did, what is left, as Markdown of at most 16 KiB. The comment is your run member's. You read the ticket and comment on it; you cannot change it.

body.description: the comment, Markdown of at most 16 KiB
